ARCHITECTURE.html.title: ProvostXInference — Architecture (as-is) | ProvostXInference API
ARCHITECTURE.html.summary: ProvostXInference — Architecture (as-is) C/C++ inference engine + C# bindings for ProvostX. A llama.cpp-only, GGUF-only execution substrate: the vendored llama.cpp tree is linked directly behind a flat C API, P/Invoked from a strict-OOP C# layer. Replaces LLamaSharp entirely — full control over batching, KV cache, vision, speculative decoding, and backend safety. ProvostXLLM consumes this library in-process and knows only this API — never llama.cpp, ONNX, or any engine internals. Layers ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ ProvostXLLM (C# — HTTP server) │ │ OpenAI API, sessions, orchestration only │ ├─────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ ProvostXInference C# (this repo) │ │ Engines facade → Abstractions → Interop │ │ Decision (ONNX judge), Encoder, watchdog │ ├─────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ libpvxinference (C++ — this repo) │ │ Model, context, pool, batched decode, │ │ sampling, embeddings, vision, spec decode, │ │ KV ops, backend safety │ ├─────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ llama.cpp (vendored submodule — FROZEN) │ │ Native inference, Metal/CUDA/Vulkan/CPU │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────┘ Dependency flow is strictly one-directional: callers touch only the Engines facade; the facade composes backend adapters into one uniform engine object; nothing below leaks upward. Native core (src/, include/) C API (pvxinference.h) — ABI v9 Flat C API, 90+ exports. Opaque handles: pvx_model_t, pvx_context_t, pvx_pool_t, pvx_conversation_t, pvx_executor_t, pvx_state_t, pvx_grammar_t, mmproj wrapper, pvx_adapter_t (LoRA), pvx_cvec_t (control vectors), pvx_tts_session_t (gen-audio). The ABI version is handshake-checked against the C# binding's ExpectedAbiVersion at engine open — mismatch refuses to load (fail-closed, never best-effort). v6 (wave 1) was append-only: pvx_spec_mode_t gained the n-gram modes, pvx_spec_params_t appends pvx_ngram_params_t, pvx_spec_capabilities_t appends spec_vision. v7 (wave 2) is append-only too: pvx_spec_mode_t gains PVX_SPEC_EAGLE3/PVX_SPEC_DFLASH, pvx_spec_params_t appends the eagle/dflash companion paths, and the new surfaces are the batched/pool-lane spec trio (pvx_conversation_spec_init/_generate_spec/_spec_stats), the per-conversation spec-session teardown hook (pvx_conversation_spec_free), and the pure JSON-schema→GBNF converter (pvx_grammar_from_json_schema, string→string, KV-neutral). v8 (wave 3) is append-only as well: pvx_pooling_type_t gains PVX_POOL_RANK (the rerank lane — classification head attached to the graph, upstream llama-server --reranking contract; pvx_rerank scores (query, doc) pairs single-shot on a fresh seq, refusal typed on any other pooling), audio input rides the mtmd surface (pvx_mtmd_supports_audio / pvx_mtmd_audio_sample_rate / pvx_executor_prompt_with_audio / pvx_conversation_prompt_with_audio — PCM F32 at the projector's native rate, no resampling in product code), TTS is a SEPARATE decode context (pvx_tts_session_create/_free/pvx_tts_generate — single-shot session, fresh sessions replay byte-identically per (text, seed), typed refusal when the mmproj has no gen-audio pipeline), LoRA adapters attach/detach on LIVE contexts (pvx_adapter_load/pvx_context_set_lora, weights-surface modifier — KV-neutral), control vectors port common_control_vector_load into src/ (pvx_control_vector_load/pvx_context_set_control_vector, same KV-neutrality), and the stats export is a snapshot copy-out. v8 wave 4 (draft-mtp, owner order 2026-10-19 17:00) is append-only too: pvx_spec_mode_t gains PVX_SPEC_MTP_DRAFT (9) and pvx_spec_params_t appends mtp_draft_path — the SEPARATE self-contained MTP head GGUF (upstream -md --spec-type draft-mtp), distinct from draft_model_path (draft-simple only) and from PVX_SPEC_MTP_AUTO (embedded nextn, which stays a typed wiring boundary). Embedded-nextn FILE CONVENTION (live-verified 2026-10-19): load_mtp reads the nextn projections from the SAME GGUF, named at the LAST TRUNK layer index (blk.{n_layer-1}.nextn.* — NOT upstream's blk.{n_layer}.*), and wants only the 6 projection tensors (eh_proj/enorm/hnorm/hc_head_norm/hc_head_down/hc_head_up); qwen4exp.attention.compress_ratios must stay n_layer_all-long (do NOT extend for the nextn layer). See memory/2026-10-19-mtp-merge-fix.md for the merge tooling. The stats export remains a snapshot (pvx_executor_stats/pvx_conversation_stats, pvx_stats_t copy-out counters, spec telemetry mirrors the spec stats). Per-engine audit + telemetry (ABI v9, owner order 2026-10-22) Append-only wave: pvx_model_params_t gains audit_path + audit_include_prompts (zeroed struct = disabled, bit-identical loads). The audit sink is PER-MODEL — own FILE* + own mutex, opened at load, closed at free; NEVER process globals (an LLM array of engines yields one audit trail per engine instance). Events are JSON lines (ts, monotonic seq, event, optional detail), flushed per line (survives hard kill): model_loaded/model_freed, context_created/freed, spec_enabled/disabled, kv_cleared/kv_shifted. Prompt TEXT is never recorded — token counts only when audit_include_prompts=1 (audit must not become a content sink). Model-wide telemetry counters ride the same struct (plain int64 bumps at the existing commit sites under the infer mutex) and are exported via pvx_engine_telemetry (pvx_engine_telemetry_t: prompt/decode/committed tokens, spec drafted/accepted, errors, contexts alive). ZERO COST when not configured: every counter bump and file write is gated behind audit.enabled — an unconfigured engine executes one branch per commit and nothing else (owner directive 10:42). Rates are derived by the caller between two snapshots; the native side stays stateless. pvxinference.cpp — core: model load, tokenize, chat template, context, conversation pool, batched + executor inference, sampling, KV ops (save/restore/copy/rewind/shift), embeddings, speculative decode, chunked decode (all decode paths split pending tokens into ≤ n_batch slices with per-slice position advance — llama_decode ABORTS beyond one batch). pvx_backend.cpp — backend safety layer (below). pvx_adapters.cpp — ABI v8 (wave 3): LoRA adapter load/attach/detach (llama_set_adapters_lora — weights-surface: live contexts, KV content untouched, serialized by the context infer_mtx) and the control-vector loader (pattern-port of the vendored common_control_vector_load_one: direction.<L> F32 1-D tensors accumulated into an n_embd × max_layer buffer; explicit out-of-range layer ends are a typed refusal, never a silent clamp). pvx_tts.cpp — ABI v8 (wave 3): speech output via the PUBLIC mtmd gen-audio helper surface (mtmd_helper_gen_audio_* — never the frozen common runtimes): a dedicated decode context on the backbone (qwen3tts — embeddings on, semantic codes through the classification-style output), our own deterministic top-k/top-p backbone sampler, raw-PCM output. The session is SINGLE-SHOT: the gen pipeline carries cross-call state inside the mtmd context, so a second generate refuses typed (tts/session-consumed) rather than degrade — fresh sessions replay byte-identically. pvx_spec_engine.* — speculative decoding: draft model (draft-simple / MTP per vendored llama.cpp support) AND n-gram modes (simple / map-k / mod / cache — no draft model, drafts from the committed stream). Decision.Engine.DecisionSessionFactory therefore constructs parameterless — the logger is a settable Logger property (quiet default) — so a facade-only caller's compiled metadata never drags the Logging namespace in (a ctor parameter's member-ref signature would do exactly that). No caller passes a logger through the ctor.

CONTRACT.html.title: ProvostXInference — Consumer Contract | ProvostXInference API
CONTRACT.html.summary: ProvostXInference — Consumer Contract Audience: developers of consumer services (ProvostXLLM, tools, tests). This is the stability promise of the caller-facing surface: what you may touch, what is guaranteed, and what is closed. Anything not listed here is internal and may change without notice. 1. The only entry point using ProvostXInference.Engines; // builder, factory, ops views, helper facades using ProvostXInference.Models; // config records, EngineStats, EngineTelemetry var engine = InferenceEngineBuilder.Gguf(modelPath) .WithGpuLayers(99) .Build(); // validated EngineRequest, fail-closed engine.Initialize(); var ops = engine.Gguf; // typed view; wrong kind => EngineKindMismatchException You reference exactly two namespaces: ProvostXInference.Engines and ProvostXInference.Models. Everything else (Implementation, Interop, SafeHandles, Logging, Abstractions) is a closed black box. 2. Engine object lifecycle contract Step Guarantee Builder.* → Build() Request validated fail-closed; bad paths/kinds/environments throw typed exceptions before any native work Initialize() Engine loads; failure leaves the engine unloaded and disposable — no partial state leaks engine.Gguf / .Decision / .Encoder Typed views over ONE graph; views wrap, never duplicate Dispose() Teardown in fixed order (pool → context → model); safe to call twice; safe after failed load 3. What IGgufEngineOps guarantees Model/context graph: chat template, tokenize/detokenize, sampling knobs, live context rebuild (RebuildContext() — old pool is disposed, state is not preserved), KV copy/clear, checkpoints (export/import byte-exact), rewind, shift. Backend probe: Backend reports the TRUTH — active specialist, effective/requested GPU layers, reduced flag. It never reports CPU for an active accelerator. Stats & telemetry (ABI v9): GetExecutorStats(executor) / GetConversationStats(conv) — per-lane counters (prompt tokens, decode steps, committed tokens, spec drafted/accepted). Snapshot copy-out; rejected drafts derive as drafted − accepted. GetEngineTelemetry() — model-wide snapshot for THIS engine instance: EngineTelemetry(PromptTokens, DecodeSteps, CommittedTokens, SpecDrafted, SpecAccepted, Errors, ContextsAlive). Pull-based and per-engine — derive rates between two snapshots in the caller; the engine keeps no rate state. Speculation: capability self-report (SpeculativeCapabilities — supported-types list, not booleans), validate/enable/disable. Unwired capability ⇒ typed NOT_SUPPORTED naming the boundary. Never a silent plain-generation fallback. Grammar: CreateGrammar (GBNF) / CreateGrammarFromJsonSchema. Every sampled token passed a grammar check (tiered rejection sampling) — output always conforms. 4. Per-engine audit trail (ABI v9) Set on the builder via ModelConfig: Setting Meaning AuditPath (null/empty = off) JSON-lines audit file for THIS engine instance only AuditIncludePrompts also record prompt token counts (never prompt text) Guarantees: Per-engine isolation: two engines in one process write two independent files and keep two independent telemetry streams. Nothing is shared (test-pinned). Events: model_loaded, model_freed, context_created, context_freed, spec_enabled, spec_disabled, kv_cleared, kv_shifted — each {"ts", "seq", "event", "detail"?}, monotonic seq, flushed per line (survives hard kill). Content policy: prompt TEXT is never recorded. Audit logs are not a content sink. Zero cost when off: unconfigured engines execute one branch per commit and nothing else — no counters, no I/O. Best-effort by design: audit is observability, never a correctness dependency; an unusable path logs a warning and disables the sink (load still succeeds). 5. Process-wide debug logging vs per-engine audit EngineLogging.SetLogFile/Enable/SetLevel routes the native DEBUG stream (llama.cpp/ggml/Metal + pvx internal logs). This is process-wide by nature — one specialist module owns the log state. Use it for diagnostics. Use AuditPath for per-engine operation trails. The two are independent channels. 6. Error contract Every failure is a typed exception carrying an error code, message, and a named boundary (e.g. spec-engine/mtp-wiring, json-schema/parse, kv/rewind): Exception When InferenceException any native-side failure (load, decode, capability, marshaled refusals) InvalidEngineRequestException builder request failed validation EngineKindMismatchException wrong ops view for the engine kind PrefillStallUnrecoveredException stall watchdog exhausted its recovery ladder Refusals are always typed and named — never empty messages, never silent fallbacks, never process aborts on supported paths. 7. Stability rules ABI handshake: the native library version must match the binding; mismatch refuses to load. Struct layouts are size-pinned by tests. Append-only ABI: new fields are appended; a zeroed struct reproduces previous behavior bit-for-bit. Consumers compiled against an older surface keep working. No silent behavior changes: every capability boundary refuses typed instead of degrading. If a feature reports supported, it is verified by tests. Config validation is fail-closed: invalid configs are rejected at build time, never clamped silently. 8. What is NOT in the contract Anything under Implementation, Interop, SafeHandles, Logging, Abstractions Internal counters not surfaced through the stats/telemetry records Native C API details (the flat pvx_* surface) — consumers go through the facade Prompt text handling inside audit trails (explicitly excluded by policy) 9. Version history ABI Consumer-visible change v8 wave-5 config verbs, stats export, audio/TTS/rerank/LoRA/cvec v9 per-engine audit (AuditPath, AuditIncludePrompts) + pvx_engine_telemetry / GetEngineTelemetry()

GETTING-STARTED.html.title: ProvostXInference — Getting Started (LLM/AI-Agent Friendly) | ProvostXInference API
GETTING-STARTED.html.summary: ProvostXInference — Getting Started (LLM/AI-Agent Friendly) Summary: Build the native C++ engine + C# bindings from a fresh clone and run all test suites. Exact commands, no fluff. Prerequisites .NET 8.0 SDK (dotnet --version → 8.x) Git (with submodule support) CMake ≥ 3.20 + a C++ toolchain (clang/gcc/MSVC) Backend SDK (optional, defaults exist): Metal is auto on macOS; CUDA or Vulkan SDKs for those backends No API keys needed — everything is local Fresh Clone → Native Build git clone --recursive https://github.com/ProvostX-Labs/ProvostXInference.git cd ProvostXInference git submodule update --init --recursive # pulls llama.cpp # macOS (Metal): cmake -B build-metal -DPVX_BACKEND_METAL=ON -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release cmake --build build-metal -j Other platforms: PVX_BACKEND_CUDA=ON (Linux/Windows), PVX_BACKEND_VULKAN=ON (Linux/Windows), or omit for CPU fallback. Run Native (C++) Tests cd build-metal DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH=. ./pvxinference_tests # basic suite DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH=. ./pvxinference_stress_tests # stress suite # Linux: use LD_LIBRARY_PATH instead of DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH Build C# Bindings cd csharp dotnet build The bindings ship a packaged native library in csharp/runtimes/<rid>/native/; on first P/Invoke, PvxNative loads the dylib from runtimes/ next to the assembly and fails fast with a descriptive DllNotFoundException on ABI mismatch (pvx_abi_version() handshake). Run C# Tests (51 xUnit tests) cd csharp DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH=../build-metal dotnet test Tests/ # macOS # Linux: LD_LIBRARY_PATH=../build-metal dotnet test Tests/ Without the env var, the packaged runtimes/ copy is used. Debug vs Release (⚠ CRITICAL) build-metal = Debug (-O0, ~70 tok/s) — dev only. Release needs: -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DGGML_METAL=ON -DGGML_METAL_EMBED_LIBRARY=ON -DGGML_ACCELERATE=ON -DGGML_BLAS=ON -DGGML_BLAS_VENDOR=Apple -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF (~89 tok/s). NEVER benchmark/ship/package a Debug dylib. PACKAGING RULE: refresh csharp/runtimes/osx-arm64/native/libpvxinference.dylib from the Release build dir before building a NuGet package. Reconfigure copied build dirs: they keep ABSOLUTE source paths — run cmake -S . -B <dir> again in the copy, or the original repo's sources get compiled silently. Never "fix" native-load issues by copying a dylib into an app root — that stale copy silently wins load order. Key Entry Points (for agents navigating the code) include/pvxinference.h — the flat C API (60+ functions); ABI version constant PVX_ABI_VERSION src/pvxinference.cpp — core (model, context, pool, executor, sampling, vision, KV) src/pvx_backend.cpp — backend probe + progressive fallback + Vulkan stale-KV flush csharp/ — .NET 8 bindings (Interop / SafeHandles / Abstractions / Implementation / Tests) tests/test_basic.cpp, tests/test_stress.cpp — native suites docs/CAPABILITY.md — capability matrix + careful-handling areas for the C# layer docs/CONFIGURATION.md — embedder params + test env vars ARCHITECTURE.md — authoritative design doc (addenda at top = current truth) ABI Rule Any native signature change: bump PVX_ABI_VERSION (header) and PvxNative.ExpectedAbiVersion (C#) in lockstep — mismatch must fail fast, not corrupt stacks. Status: Current as of 2026-10-11.

README.html.title: ProvostXInference | ProvostXInference API
README.html.summary:
ProvostXInference C/C++ inference engine + C# bindings for ProvostX — a llama.cpp-only, GGUF-only execution substrate behind a strict-OOP C# facade. Replaces LLamaSharp entirely. Why this repo Full control of the native seam — llama.cpp linked directly behind a flat C API; batching, KV cache, vision, speculative decoding and backend safety are ours, not a wrapper's. Fail-closed everywhere — typed errors with named boundaries; unknown capabilities refuse, they never silently degrade. ABI version handshake at load; struct layouts test-pinned. Per-engine observability — each engine instance can carry its own JSON-lines audit trail and model-wide telemetry snapshot; zero cost when unconfigured. Features Area What you get Key types Model loading GGUF, GPU layers, flash attention, KV quant (F16/Q8_0/Q4_0) ModelConfig, NativeInferenceModel Generation Prompt → infer → sample loop, full sampling pipeline (wave-5 verbs: dry, xtc, top-n-sigma, mirostat) IStandardExecutor, SamplingConfig Batched 4+ conversations in ONE decode; pre-allocated pool, lease/return with KV cleanup IConversationPool, IConversation Vision mmproj + image prompt splice (MTMD) IVisionEncoder Embeddings mean/CLS/last pooling; encoder models (MiniLM/BERT) routed by architecture GetEmbeddings Speculative draft-simple, n-gram family, EAGLE3, draft-MTP (incl. multi-block chain heads) SpeculativeConfig Audio / TTS audio input (PCM F32), speech output on gen-audio pipelines PromptWithAudio, ITtsSession Rerank / LoRA / cvec single-shot rerank; live LoRA attach; control vectors Rerank, SetAdapters Audit + telemetry per-engine JSON-lines audit trail; model-wide counters; zero-cost when off ModelConfig.AuditPath, GetEngineTelemetry() Grammar GBNF + JSON-schema→GBNF converter; tiered rejection sampling CreateGrammar, CreateGrammarFromJsonSchema Quickstart Native library (macOS Metal example; see CI matrix for Linux/Windows backends): git submodule update --init --recursive cmake -B build-metal -DPVX_BACKEND_METAL=ON -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release cmake --build build-metal -j ctest --test-dir build-metal --output-on-failure # model-gated legs skip without models C# bindings (stage the built dylib where the resolver looks): mkdir -p csharp/runtimes/osx-arm64/native cp build-metal/libpvxinference.dylib csharp/runtimes/osx-arm64/native/ cd csharp dotnet test Tests/ # 252 tests; live lanes skip typed when no model fixture is present Minimal consumer code (from the verified consumer harness): var engine = InferenceEngineBuilder.Gguf(modelPath).Build(); engine.Initialize(); var exec = engine.Gguf.CreateExecutor(); exec.Prompt("The capital of France is"); exec.Infer(); var token = exec.Sample(new SamplingConfig { Temperature = 0.3f }); Backend / capability matrix RID slice Specialist Built by osx-arm64 metal (+ generic cpu) CI win-arm64 cpu (generic payload) CI win-x64 cuda + vulkan CI linux-x64 cuda + vulkan CI linux-arm64 source-build + ORT documented path No native binaries are checked in — CI builds every slice at pack time (keeps compiler-baked build paths out of the repository). The managed resolver picks the specialist for the host OS; the cpu specialist falls back to the generic payload name. Architecture graph TD LLM[ProvostXLLM — orchestration only] --> FACADE[Engines facade
Builder → Factory → ops views] FACADE --> IMPL[Implementation — native wrappers, engine selection] IMPL --> INTEROP[Interop — per-handle dispatch, ABI handshake] INTEROP --> NATIVE[libpvxinference — C API: model, context, pool,
batched decode, sampling, embeddings, vision, spec, KV, audit] NATIVE --> LLAMA[llama.cpp — vendored, frozen] Details: ARCHITECTURE.md · Consumer contract: CONTRACT.md Documentation Document Content CONTRACT.md Consumer contract — what you may touch, what is guaranteed ARCHITECTURE.md As-is architecture, all layers, ABI waves docs/CAPABILITY.md Capability matrix + careful-handling areas docs/CONFIGURATION.md Configuration reference GETTING-STARTED.md Getting started docs/api-glossary.md Every public type explained docs/faq.md Frequently asked questions TEST-MATRIX-2026-10-18.md Real-model verification matrix License MIT — see LICENSE. TEST-EVIDENCE-spec.html.title: Speculative decoding test evidence (owner-requested, 2026-10-11 23:27) | ProvostXInference API
TEST-EVIDENCE-spec.html.summary: Speculative decoding test evidence (owner-requested, 2026-10-11 23:27) All runs: llama-cli (vendored build-spec, metal), temp 0. draft_simple — WORKS Target Llama-3.2-3B-Q4_K_M + draft Llama-3.2-1B-Q4_K_M: clean generation. Baseline 168.9 t/s vs draft ~161–162 t/s → NO gain on a fast small target (draft overhead ≥ savings at 3B speeds). Expected physics; use spec on bigger/slower targets. draft_mtp — WORKS, real speedup Model: unsloth/Qwen3.5-9B-MTP-GGUF (Qwen3.5-9B-Q4_K_M.gguf, 5.9 GB, MTP tensors embedded). Short gen (96 tok): baseline 63.1 t/s → MTP 90.3 t/s (+43%) Long gen (256 tok): baseline 82.2 t/s → MTP 108.1 t/s (+31%) Conclusion: ~1.3–1.4× on Qwen3.5-9B via --spec-type draft-mtp. No second model needed. Notes for ABI wiring CLI flag: --spec-type draft-mtp (enum: none, draft-simple, draft-eagle3, draft-mtp, draft-dflash, draft-dspark, ngram-*). Our other local GGUFs (Qwen3-8B, Llama-3.2-3B, Qwen3.6-35B) have NO nextn tensors → engine capability discovery must read GGUF metadata (arch + nextn tensor presence), not assume. EAGLE3/DFLASH/DSpark drafts are per-target companions; drafts need GGUF conversion against the target (docs/speculative.md has exact commands; EAGLE3 pairs AngelSlim/Qwen3-8B_eagle3 with our local Qwen3-8B).

Notable failures (exact evidence) — 1 & 2 FIXED 2026-10-18 am, re-verified live 1. FIXED — Backend probe misreported Metal as CPU (all GGUF models, default AND explicit metal specialist) Evidence: backend=CPU probePassed=True gpuLayers eff/req=0/0 reduced=False activeSpecialist=(platform-default) — identical with WithGpuLayers(99) and with explicit WithEngineId("metal"). Metal is demonstrably active (embedded metal lib loads; MTL0 compute buffers allocated; splits=2 graphs), so this is a misreport, not a CPU-only run. Root cause (code-level): src/pvx_backend.cpp detect_backend() greps device names for "Metal", but the vendored ggml names the metal device GGML_METAL_NAME="MTL" → "MTL0" (see llama.cpp/ggml/src/ggml-metal/ggml-metal.cpp:15). strstr("MTL0","Metal") never matches → every probe fell through to PVX_BACKEND_CPU. Second defect in the same slice: original_gpu_layers/effective_gpu_layers/gpu_layers_reduced were only written by pvx_create_context_safe(), which the C# facade path never uses (it calls per-handle pvx_create_context directly), so BackendInfo gpu-layer visibility was structurally 0/0 for every facade-created engine. Fix: detection now skips CPU-class devices and matches the stable vendor-tag device ids (MTL/Metal, CUDA, Vulkan); an unrecognized accelerator reports its raw ggml device name (PVX_BACKEND_GPU_OTHER) instead of lying "CPU". gpu-layer fields are computed by pvx_backend_fill_profile() — called from pvx_create_context (every facade path) and re-run by pvx_probe_backend (requested = model's load-time config; effective = min(requested, n_layer+1), 0 on a CPU verdict). Re-verification (large-memory host, results-verify.txt + flash-probe.final.log): RESULT|…/backend-probe-gpu99|PASS|gpuLayers req=99 → backend=Metal probePassed=True eff/req=29/99 reduced=True (Llama-3B); identical PASS on Qwen3.5-4B (33/99), Qwen3.6-35B (41/99), Flash-Next (49/99). The in-lane backend-probe row flipped too: backend=Metal probePassed=True gpuLayers eff/req=29/-1 reduced=False. C# IGgufEngineOps.Backend reports the truth through the facade. 2. FIXED — pvx_get_embeddings SEGFAULTED on generative models with MEAN pooling (dense AND hybrid) Evidence: IInferenceModel.GetEmbeddings with a MEAN-pooling context on Llama-3.2-3B (dense) and Qwen3.5-4B (hybrid) → process dies with SIGSEGV (rc=139), reproducible both when pooling is set at load and via RebuildContext; lldb: EXC_BAD_ACCESS (code=1, address=0x10), faulting instruction ldr x8, [x0, #0x10] (null-object deref) immediately after the embeddings forward completes (sched_reserve printed, graph ran). RebuildContext(Mean) + dispose WITHOUT calling GetEmbeddings = PASS (no crash) — the fault is inside the native embeddings read path, not teardown. Encoder-arch embeddings (MiniLM) PASS, so the crash is specific to generative (causal) models + pooling. Contract angle: a pooling request on a causal model should be a typed error (fail-closed), never a segv. All four gguf-all runs ended rc=139 at this row before the row was split into an isolated subprocess test. Root cause: the embeddings path called llama_encode FIRST and fell back to llama_decode on error. llama_encode on a decoder-only model builds an ENCODER graph on a causal arch and dies with the observed EXC_BAD_ACCESS (address=0x10) right after sched_reserve (the graph path the model does not define). MiniLM survived because it takes the encode path for the right reason. Fix: encode-vs-decode is now routed by the model's own architecture (llama_model_has_encoder/has_decoder; typed NOT_SUPPORTED if a model exposes neither). Extraction fails CLOSED (typed error) when no embedding source produces data. Re-verification (large-memory host, results-verify.txt / results-verify3.txt): pre-fix repro: embed-isolate L3B load rc=139, embed-isolate Q35 load rc=139. Post-fix: RESULT|Llama-3.2-3B/embed-isolate-load|PASS|mean-pooling embeddings dim=3072 L2=1.00 sim=0.819 > disim=0.548 (load AND rebuild); Qwen3.5-4B dim=2560 … sim=0.723 > disim=0.476; Qwen3.6-35B dim=2048 … sim=0.784 > disim=0.568; MiniLM unchanged (dim=384). Flash-Next (honest boundary, NOT a silent pass): the merged Q5_K_M file reports n_embd_out=10240 vs n_embd=2560 (4-way multi-token output head). llama.cpp's internal MEAN extraction would read 10240 floats from a 2560-wide pooled tensor and its upstream bounds assert ABORTED the process (observed rc=134 on the first verify round). Now a typed fail-closed refusal BEFORE any decode: InferenceException[code=7]: NOT_SUPPORTED: embeddings: model's output head (n_embd_out=10240) differs from its hidden state (n_embd=2560) - merged multi-token output head cannot be pooled honestly (boundary: embeddings/pooling) — both at-load and after RebuildContext, rc=0, deterministic dispose (first verify round also exposed a HARNESS lifecycle bug: the undisposed engine on the exception path raced finalizers at exit and tripped the known metal teardown assert — scratch harness fixed to dispose + emit a TYPED verdict; native contract unchanged). 3. FIXED (message plumbing) — MTP wiring boundary (expected refusal, now with a named reason) Evidence (all models): EnableSpeculation(Mtp) → InferenceException[code=7]: NOT_SUPPORTED: PVX_SPEC_MTP_AUTO not wired in this build: MTP drafting requires LLAMA_CONTEXT_TYPE_MTP context plumbing + nextn hidden-state extraction this specialist does not construct yet; the mtp capability reports model-level presence honestly (boundary: spec-engine/mtp-wiring). ActiveSpeculation stays null after the failed enable; GenerateSpeculative without a session → typed NOT_SUPPORTED: no spec session on this executor (boundary: spec-engine/session). No model on disk reports the mtp capability bit (the Q5_K_M merged Flash-Next GGUF carries no nextn tensors; the Q8 MTP sidecar exists on disk but has no load path through this API). Minor (FIXED): ValidateSpeculation(Mtp) on non-mtp models used to throw code 7 with an empty message string (NOT_SUPPORTED: ). Root cause was twofold: the native pvx_model_spec_validate set NO reason string, and the C# layer passed a MODEL handle to pvx_last_error (a CONTEXT-handle function — wrong struct layout). Fix (ABI v5): new pvx_model_last_error(model) export + native validate writes model-scoped reasons + C# ThrowIfModelError retrieves them. Re-verified: Validate(Mtp)=typed: InferenceException[code=7]: NOT_SUPPORTED: model has no MTP capability (no nextn tensors in the GGUF; boundary: spec-engine/capability) (the local unit test now also asserts a non-empty reason). 4. Data observation (not an engine bug) The file named Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf on disk has a Qwen-style special vocabulary (generates </im_start/> / </im_end/> markers under its own chat template). Handled fine by the engine; flagged because the file name does not match its tokenizer family. Verified-good seams (one-liners) Fail-closed everywhere it was probed: bad model path → InferenceException[code=3] LOAD_FAILED; unknown specialist id → typed resolver refusal listing metal, cuda, vulkan; out-of-range KvClearSeq → INVALID_ARG; hybrid rewind → REWIND_UNSUPPORTED (code 8, seq_rm refused by memory); spec boundaries all typed with named boundaries. KV portability is real: export/import checkpoint restored exact token counts on every arch including the 125 GiB Flash-Next (118 MB checkpoint) and both hybrids. Speculative draft-simple is token-exact vs the plain loop (12/12), streams via onToken (stream == returned), reports ActiveSpeculation after enable, and tears down typed. Continuous batching via pool leases + InferAll kept all concurrent conversations progressing on every model (incl. batch16k prefill on Flash-Next). Grammar (GBNF) sampling is character-position correct: single-token pieces like a,p,pl,e are legal mid-word continuations; every emitted sequence was strictly grammar-constrained on all four GGUF models. Vision lane works end-to-end end through the facade (mmproj load → <__media__> splice → prefill 20 tok → generation), with a real 64×64 PNG; the repo-root test_image.png (168 bytes) is a stub, not a valid image. Decision lane judges via the facade with truthful activeProvider=cpu reporting. NOT-RUN (with reasons) Flash-Next IQ4_XS sharded variant — the Q5_K_M merged file served the Flash lane; the 93 GiB 3-shard IQ4_XS was not loaded (redundant lane, RAM/time budget; no behavioral difference expected — same arch/family). MTP draft model live run — native MTP is a typed NOT_SUPPORTED boundary in this build (verified); the on-disk MTP sidecar (mtp-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Q8_0.gguf) and no other draft sidecar has a load path through the engine facade; no fake pass claimed. Spec draft-exactness for the Qwen models — no same-vocab-family small draft GGUF exists on disk (spec-test/ holds only a tokenizer.json); token-exactness was instead proven on the Llama-3.2 3B+1B pair. Vision on 35B/Flash — no matching mmproj projector on disk for those models (the available projector is Qwen3.5-4B-specific). Repro Harness (scratch, outside the repo): facade-driven C# console app + bash driver; per-load RAM gate; fresh Release dylib pinned via runtimes-copy sha. Raw logs and RESULT lines preserved under the scratch logs dir (results*.txt, *.log). Fix-round drivers (same harness, large-memory host): run-repro.sh → results-repro.txt (pre-fix failures), run-verify.sh → results-verify.txt (probe ×4, embed ×4, gguf-all L3B/Q35/35B), run-verify2.sh/run-verify3.sh (Flash typed-refusal + regression), flash-probe.final.log. Note on row 12 (vision) — pre-existing flake, unchanged by the fix round An intermittent first-sample flake exists on the Qwen3.5-4B vision lane: in some runs the first conv.Sample returns −1/EOS and the row emits genTokens=0 (observed in pre-fix pass2 results2.txt, pre-fix pass3 results3.txt FAIL+PASS pair, and once in the fix-round verify run). Identical evidence string in pre- and post-fix code → pre-existing, unrelated to the three fixed failures; not investigated this round. The PASS evidence stands from the runs where generation started.

api/ProvostXInference.Decision.Engine.Ju.title: Class JudgeTokenizer | ProvostXInference API
api/ProvostXInference.Decision.Engine.Ju.summary: Class JudgeTokenizer Deterministic BPE tokenizer for the Laya judge models (mmBERT vocabulary, HuggingFace tokenizer.json format: BPE model + Replace(" " → "▁") normalizer + Metaspace pre-tokenizer, add_special_tokens=False semantics — no BOS/EOS post-processing; the judge sequence builder places CLS/SEP itself). Pipeline (replicates the training tokenizer byte-for-byte): 1. added-token extraction (longest match, pre-normalization, per segment), 2. normalization: " " → "▁" per non-added segment, 3. Metaspace pre-tokenization: prepend "▁" when the segment does not start with it, then split BEFORE every "▁" (each "▁" begins a piece), 4. greedy lowest-rank BPE merges per piece (pairs of in-vocab symbols only), 5. unknown symbols: byte fallback ("<0xXX>" tokens), then <unk> (consecutive unknowns fused). Thread-safe: all mutable state is ConcurrentDictionary caches; encoding is a pure function of the input text. Deterministic: no RNG, no time, no IO after construction. Verified against the training pipeline on the committed vector fixture (Tests/Assets/judge/tok-vectors.json). api/ProvostXInference.Decision.Engine.ht.title: Namespace ProvostXInference.Decision.Engine | ProvostXInference API
api/ProvostXInference.Decision.Engine.ht.summary: Namespace ProvostXInference.Decision.Engine Classes DecisionAssetCatalog Resolves the judge ASSET files (tokenizer.json, judge-spec-*.json) for one configured judge model. Resolution order (first hit wins): 1. model config "file" SIBLING directory (a bundled model dir ships both), 2. the server root's assets/models/judge/ directory, 3. next to the server binary (Assets/models/judge copied at build/pack time). Spec file per record kind: judge-spec-shell.json / judge-spec-process.json. Pure resolver — performs no IO beyond existence checks at Resolve time. DecisionHeaderReader Wave-2 ONNX header validation: a REAL protobuf scan of the ModelProto wire — ir_version (field 1, varint), the graph message (field 7) with its input (field 11) and output (field 12) ValueInfoProto names, and opset_import presence (field 8). Long initializers are SKIPPED by seek (never read into memory), so a 500MB+ model validates in milliseconds. Any structural violation throws — the load state machine maps that to fail-closed model_invalid before any session init is attempted. Wire-format reference: developers.onnxruntime.ai/onnx/proto (ModelProto, GraphProto, ValueInfoProto field tables). Pure scanner — no state. DecisionRecord One judged decision record, validated and normalized (parser → executor boundary). SHELL records carry command+cwd; PROCESS records carry the os/exe/chain/cmd/net/writes tuple. The untrusted SHELL "purpose" field deliberately has NO field here — it is echoed in audit logs only and never reaches decision input. DecisionSession ONE loaded ONNX judge model ready for batch inference: the ORT session (selected execution provider recorded), the tokenizer, the sequence spec, and the row collation + decode that mirrors the training evaluation exactly. Disposal releases the session. NOT thread-safe per instance beyond the session's own safety — the executor serializes inference per engine. Decode (training-eval semantics, per question row k = option count): choice → argmax over the k class logits → JudgeAction (allow/sandbox/deny); noul → softmax over 2, P(true) = NeedsSandbox; score → softmax over 5, expected value = Risk (0..4); confidence → max class probability after temperature scaling (0..1). The Jev raw wire (JudgeQuestionSet) decodes ARBITRARY caller questions instead: choice → argmax option label + per-option probabilities, score → expected level value + level-index probabilities, noul → P(true) — same softmax/temperature machinery, no escalation. DecisionSessionFactory Creates DecisionSessions for a judge model file: builds the ORT session options (full graph optimization, matching the training runtime) and walks the parsed ExecutionProviderChain in preference order (LLM-10 per-OS chains). EP FALLBACK RULE: a provider that fails to initialize (not bundled, driver/library problems, unsupported ops) degrades to the next entry — CPU is always the terminal fallback and is the only provider REQUIRED to work. The session's ACTUALLY-active provider is read back from the runtime (a silent ORT fallback to CPU counts as a fallback, not as GPU) and recorded so /pvx/health `active_execution_provider` is truthful. One factory per host; thread-safe (stateless beyond the injected option applier). DecisionTestSupport Test-support surface for the decision engine slice (Inference-side, consumed by both repos' test suites): opens an ORT session with ONE pinned provider. Keeping the only direct ORT-construction site inside ProvostXInference is the LLM→Inference extraction contract — LLM-side code references no ORT types. EpAttempt One candidate configuration for an EP session init: a label for diagnostics and the options mutation it applies. Ordered — first that successfully creates a session wins. ExecutionProviderChain Parsed execution-provider chain for a decision (judge) model (e.g. "cpu", "coreml->cpu", "cuda->cpu"). First entry is the preferred provider; later entries are fallbacks. Unknown names fail config validation loudly (the parser throws) — silent CPU fallback for typos is a misconfiguration hazard. ExecutionProviderOptionsApplier Per-EP session-option presets (LLM-10): each configured chain entry may need provider-specific session options (CUDA device id, DirectML device id, ROCm device id, OpenVINO device type, CoreML flags). Every preset list ends with a PLAIN name-append fallback so a quirk mismatch never fails an otherwise loadable provider — remaining failures fall down the chain to cpu (never fail when cpu works). Instance type, no state — cheap to construct, injectable. JudgeModelNotReadyException Typed fail-closed judge error: every judge endpoint maps this to HTTP 503 with a machine-readable code — NEVER to a 200/allow verdict. Codes: "model_unloaded" (judge engine present but not loaded) and "model_missing" (no judge model configured/registered for the requested id). JudgeNumericsGate Canonical numerics gate (LLM-10): before a NON-CPU execution provider is accepted, the judge model must reproduce the canonical wave-4 anchor (the destructive `dd` deny — recorded on the CPU EP: deny EXACT, conf ≈ 0.9231, risk ≈ 3.128) within tolerance. A GPU/CoreML EP that loads but drifts the anchors is REJECTED and the chain continues to the next provider (cpu always terminates). Fail-closed: gate evaluation errors count as drift. JudgeOption One rendered option of a judge question: its answer label and its criterion description (null = no description — rendered as the bare label). Option ORDER is decision-meaningful (argmax index → label). Pure data. JudgeQuestionAnswer ONE raw model answer for one Jev question (session decode → response mapper boundary). RAW semantics: the model's argmax choice / expected score / noul probability — NO risk-escalation rule applied (the escalation owner is JudgeVerdictMapper on the enriched arms; the raw wire stays raw). Field populations per type: choice → Choice + Confidence + Probabilities; score → Score + Confidence + Probabilities (level-index keyed) + Legend; noul → Noul. Pure data. JudgeQuestionAnswerSet The raw answers for ONE Jev request (one state), in question order, plus the USAGE inputs: the tokenized state length (actual tokenizer count of the serialized state — the usage.input_tokens definition) and the question count (the usage.output_tokens definition: one answer per question). Pure data. JudgeQuestionDef One typed judge question as trained (id, type, instructions, ordered options). Pure data — the judge spec carries these in the exact training order (action, needs_sandbox, risk_level). JudgeQuestionRowSet Encoded question rows for ONE Jev state + the pre-truncation token count of the serialized state (usage.input_tokens source). One row per question, in question order. Pure data. JudgeRowEncoding Encoded ONE question row of a judge record: token ids, marker (MASK) offsets, and the question's type. One record → one row per question, in question order. Pure data. JudgeScore Raw model output for one judged record (executor → response mapper boundary). The mapper owns the risk-escalation rule; the executor reports raw scores only. JudgeSequenceEncoder Builds judge model input rows from validated DecisionRecords: serializes the record EXACTLY as the training pipeline did (compact JSON with the mask token stripped), then assembles [CLS] {type} question: {instructions} [SEP] [MASK] opt0 [MASK] opt1 ... [SEP] {state} [SEP] per question, with the state tail capped to the sequence budget. Mirrors the training sequence builder (head budget 256, options capped at 48 tokens each) against the committed fixtures (Tests/Assets/judge/seq-fixtures.json). One encoder per judge model spec; thread-safe (stateless + immutable fields). JudgeSequenceSpec The FULL serialized inference specification for one judge model: record kind, sequence budget (max_len/head_max_len exactly as trained), the confidence temperatures fitted at export time, and the three typed questions in training order. Loaded from a spec JSON (Assets/models/judge/judge-spec-*.json) — the questions MUST match the training questions verbatim or the model scores text it was never trained on. JudgeStateQuestions One decision-engine question batch on the Jev wire: the SERIALIZED state text (rule owned by the server layer's state serializer — the engine plane only sees text) and the typed questions to answer. Questions = null → the judge's CANONICAL trained question set (the loaded session's spec — our additive default for omitted questions; real Jev requires questions). One request → one answer set. Pure data. JudgeTokenizer Deterministic BPE tokenizer for the Laya judge models (mmBERT vocabulary, HuggingFace tokenizer.json format: BPE model + Replace(" " → "▁") normalizer + Metaspace pre-tokenizer, add_special_tokens=False semantics — no BOS/EOS post-processing; the judge sequence builder places CLS/SEP itself). Pipeline (replicates the training tokenizer byte-for-byte): 1. added-token extraction (longest match, pre-normalization, per segment), 2. normalization: " " → "▁" per non-added segment, 3. Metaspace pre-tokenization: prepend "▁" when the segment does not start with it, then split BEFORE every "▁" (each "▁" begins a piece), 4. greedy lowest-rank BPE merges per piece (pairs of in-vocab symbols only), 5. unknown symbols: byte fallback ("<0xXX>" tokens), then <unk> (consecutive unknowns fused). Thread-safe: all mutable state is ConcurrentDictionary caches; encoding is a pure function of the input text. Deterministic: no RNG, no time, no IO after construction. Verified against the training pipeline on the committed vector fixture (Tests/Assets/judge/tok-vectors.json). OsExecutionProviderDefaultSource Per-OS default EP chains (LLM-10): macOS coreml→cpu, Windows directml→cpu, Linux cuda→rocm→openvino→cpu — first available wins at session init; cpu is always the terminal fallback. An injected osOverride keeps the mapping testable without touching the real host OS. Enums JudgeAction Judge verdict actions. The FINAL action in the wire response is produced by JudgeVerdictMapper, which owns the risk-escalation rule — the executor's raw action may be upgraded (allow → require_approval) but never downgraded. JudgeQuestionType Judge question types, numbered EXACTLY as the judge models were trained (laya QTYPES): choice=0, score=1, noul=2. The value feeds the model's qtype input — never renumber. JudgeRecordKind Discriminator for judge decision records on the decision-engine wire /v1/systemone (two record kinds on the same endpoint — the enriched arms; the raw Jev shape carries a free-form state instead). OnnxExecutionProvider Execution providers for decision (judge) models. The chain is parsed and validated at config time so unknown names fail loudly. Per-OS: CoreML (macOS), DirectML (Windows), CUDA/ROCm/OpenVINO (Linux) — cpu is always the terminal fallback.

api/ProvostXInference.Implementation.Chu.title: Class ChunkedStallSafePrefillRunner | ProvostXInference API
api/ProvostXInference.Implementation.Chu.summary: Class ChunkedStallSafePrefillRunner Engine-level stall-safe chunked prefill layer (INF BL-33). Independent of downstream orchestration AND backend-independent by construction: it leases conversations from the injected pool, commits the prompt in chunks via PromptTokens, and times each chunk commit with pure wall-clock around the synchronous native prompt call — the pvxinference substrate dispatches to whatever backend is compiled in (metal / cuda / vulkan / cpu), and this layer never knows or cares which. No backend timing hook exists or is required; wall-clock is the sole detection mechanism, so detection behaves identically on every backend. On stall it walks the configured recovery ladder (fresh-slot retry → smaller-chunk retry → draft/ngram disabled → fail loud). Honesty notes: - A fresh-slot retry re-prefills the committed prefix on the new slot (the new slot starts with an empty KV), so it is correct, not cheap. - The draft/ngram-disabled step suspends the speculative session through a constructor-injected ISpeculationSuspender (real native wiring: pvx_executor_spec_free via ExecutorSpeculationSuspender). When no suspender is wired, that step fails closed with the typed unrecovered error naming the missing seam — never a silent skip. - With Enabled = false the runner performs a single plain prompt commit (watchdog fully inert). api/ProvostXInference.Implementation.htm.summary: Namespace ProvostXInference.Implementation Classes ChunkedStallSafePrefillRunner Engine-level stall-safe chunked prefill layer (INF BL-33). Independent of downstream orchestration AND backend-independent by construction: it leases conversations from the injected pool, commits the prompt in chunks via PromptTokens, and times each chunk commit with pure wall-clock around the synchronous native prompt call — the pvxinference substrate dispatches to whatever backend is compiled in (metal / cuda / vulkan / cpu), and this layer never knows or cares which. No backend timing hook exists or is required; wall-clock is the sole detection mechanism, so detection behaves identically on every backend. On stall it walks the configured recovery ladder (fresh-slot retry → smaller-chunk retry → draft/ngram disabled → fail loud). Honesty notes: - A fresh-slot retry re-prefills the committed prefix on the new slot (the new slot starts with an empty KV), so it is correct, not cheap. - The draft/ngram-disabled step suspends the speculative session through a constructor-injected ISpeculationSuspender (real native wiring: pvx_executor_spec_free via ExecutorSpeculationSuspender). When no suspender is wired, that step fails closed with the typed unrecovered error naming the missing seam — never a silent skip. - With Enabled = false the runner performs a single plain prompt commit (watchdog fully inert). ExecutorSpeculationSuspender Runtime draft/ngram suspension backed by the executor's native speculative-session teardown (pvx_executor_spec_free; INF BL-33b). Idempotent by construction — the native teardown is already idempotent and the suspension is recorded so a second Suspend is a managed no-op. GgufMetadataRepair GGUF tokenizer-metadata repair (owner 2026-10-06): some HuggingFace GGUFs omit the EOS token from tokenizer.ggml.special_eog_ids — the engine's native EOS stop then never fires and generation runs past end-of-turn. The native pvx_repair_eog_metadata rewrites the METADATA ONLY (weights stream-copied byte-for-byte); this is the public managed facade over it. Dispatches on the ACTIVE engine's per-handle dispatch tables (BL-02). NativeControlVector ABI v8 (wave 3, feature 10): wraps a pvx_cvec_t (control-vector direction file). Loaded via NativeInferenceModel.CreateControlVector (n_embd-matched, typed refusal naming both dims on mismatch); all dispatch goes through the OWNING ENGINE's per-handle tables. Applied to contexts via NativeInferenceContext.SetControlVector; weights-surface modifier (KV-neutral, live attach/detach). NativeConversation Wraps a leased pvx_conversation_t. Does NOT own the handle — the pool does. Dispose() returns it to the pool if not already returned. All calls dispatch on the OWNING ENGINE's per-handle tables (carried from the pool at lease). NativeConversationPool Wraps a native pvx_pool_t. All calls dispatch on the OWNING ENGINE's per-handle tables (flowed from the context's model); a leased conversation carries the same tables for its own calls. NativeConversationSpecSession Speculative session bound to ONE pooled conversation (ABI v7, feature 5): enable/generate/stats over pvx_conversation_spec_*, with the active-config mirror kept honest by routing every mutation through Enable/Disable below (same discipline as the executor lane). The native pool-return/teardown paths free the session natively; ProvostXInference.Implementation.NativeConversationSpecSession.OnReturned() clears the managed mirror so it can never report a phantom session. NativeConversationState Wraps a conversation state (pvx_conversation_save). Token count queries dispatch on the OWNING ENGINE's per-handle tables (constructor-injected, carried from the conversation at save time). NativeGrammar Wraps a pvx_grammar_t. Created through — and dispatching on — the OWNING MODEL ENGINE's per-handle tables. NativeInferenceBackend Backend safety layer (pvx_probe_backend + queries). The probe is context-anchored and dispatches on the OWNING CONTEXT ENGINE's per-handle tables; the process-wide queries dispatch on the ACTIVE engine — a no-op passthrough until a model load activates it. NativeInferenceContext Wraps a native pvx_context_t. All calls dispatch on the OWNING MODEL ENGINE's per-handle tables (injected via the model). NativeInferenceModel Wraps a native pvx_model_t. Factory: Load(). BL-02: EVERY pvx_* call this model (and everything created from it) makes is dispatched through the OWNING ENGINE's per-handle dispatch tables — resolved once at engine open and injected down the whole object graph; no global P/Invoke routing. NativeInferenceState Wraps a pvx_state_t (pvx_state_save). Token count queries dispatch on the OWNING ENGINE's per-handle tables (constructor-injected). NativeLoraAdapter ABI v8 (wave 3, feature 9): wraps a pvx_adapter_t (LoRA). Loaded via NativeInferenceModel.CreateLoraAdapter (arch-matched, typed on mismatch); all dispatch goes through the OWNING ENGINE's per-handle tables. Attached to contexts via NativeInferenceContext.SetAdapters; adapters are freed on Dispose (and by the model at its teardown — native contract). NativeStandardExecutor Wraps a pvx_executor_t (standard, non-batched path). All calls dispatch on the OWNING ENGINE's per-handle tables (flowed from the context). NativeTtsSession ABI v8 (wave 3, feature 7): wraps a pvx_tts_session_t — a SEPARATE decode context on the backbone speech model plus a gen-audio mmproj (never a conversation context; KV-neutral by construction). All calls dispatch on the OWNING ENGINE's per-handle tables. NativeVisionEncoder Wraps an mmproj context for vision/image encoding. All calls dispatch on the OWNING ENGINE's per-handle tables (constructor-injected). PvxDefaultEngineSelector Platform default engine selection — used when the model config leaves the engine field unset: macOS resolves to the metal specialist; Windows/Linux prefer cuda when its specialist file ships, else vulkan, else the cpu engine (every platform can build a CPU specialist); fail-closed (typed error, no silent fallback) when none is installed. The OS identity is constructor-injected (same probe family the selector matrix consults — no hidden environment dependence). Stateless utility — no mutable state. RollingPrefillStallDetector Rolling-median stall detector (INF BL-33). A chunk is a stall when its wall exceeds GapMultiplier × the rolling median of the recent baseline window. The detector is silent (never a stall) until the baseline holds at least MinBaselineSamples clean observations — the first chunks of a prefill cannot be judged against an empty baseline. StallRecoveryLadder Recovery ladder for the stall-safe prefill layer (INF BL-33). Owns the configured step order and the retry budget; returns the step for a given 0-based retry attempt and fails closed when the budget is exhausted (the caller is expected to throw the typed unrecovered error then — the ladder itself never invents steps). SystemChunkWallClock Production wall clock backed by the injected TimeProvider (constructor injection, no statics — INF BL-33).

api/ProvostXInference.Models.Speculative.summary: Enum SpeculativeMode Speculative-decoding mode, values mirror pvx_spec_mode_t exactly. Namespace: ProvostXInference.Models Assembly: ProvostXInference.dll Syntax public enum SpeculativeMode Fields Name Description Dflash ABI v7 — DFlash block-diffusion fused drafting (upstream draft-dflash). Requires a dflash companion GGUF (DflashCompanionPath); metadata validated, drafting unwired — typed boundary. Draft Second draft model (upstream draft-simple) — requires a draft_simple capability plus a user-provided DraftModelPath. Eagle3 ABI v7 — EAGLE3 companion draft decoder fed (token, g_embd) pairs from target layer features (upstream draft-eagle3). Requires an eagle3 companion GGUF (EagleCompanionPath); sequential executor lane only — the batched/pool lane refuses typed. Mtp Model-native MTP drafting — requires an mtp capability; enabling currently fails typed NOT_SUPPORTED while the MTP wiring boundary stands. MtpDraft ABI v8 wave 4 — SEPARATE self-contained draft-MTP head GGUF (upstream draft-mtp, llama.cpp PR #28243; qwen4exp-family targets). Requires an MTP head GGUF (MtpDraftPath — never DraftModelPath); drafts on the target trunk's nextn embeddings, verified greedy-exact by the target. Sequential executor lane only — the batched/pool lane refuses typed. NgramCache ABI v6 — static (file) + dynamic token-probability caches (upstream ngram-cache). NgramMapK ABI v6 — n-gram -> m-gram map with per-value accept statistics (upstream ngram-map-k). NgramMod ABI v6 — MOD: hashed (n-1)-suffix match, one deviation (upstream ngram-mod). NgramSimple ABI v6 — n-gram drafting from the committed stream: no draft model. History-pattern lookup (upstream ngram-simple). Off

Defaults follow the owner decision: multiplier 5 over the rolling median chunk wall, 3 retries, the full four-step recovery ladder. TtsRequest ABI v8 (wave 3, feature 7): TTS knobs. Zero values select the per-model upstream defaults (native mtmd_gen_inp_default); Seed == uint.MaxValue selects a random draw (fixed seeds replay byte-identically). TtsResult TTS generation result: raw PCM F32 mono at the pipeline rate. Enums KvOverrideTag Tag for a GGUF metadata override value (BL-21b wave-5). KvType Managed enum mirroring PvxKvType. PoolingType Managed enum mirroring PvxPoolingType. PrefillRecoveryStep Recovery-ladder step executed after a detected prefill stall (stall-safe prefill layer, INF BL-33). Ordered from cheapest to fail-loud; the ladder always terminates in FailLoud so a persistently stalling prefill never spins silently. PvxEngineSelectionError Typed failure of engine-selection validation (fail-closed contract — every invalid pair or unknown id resolves to one of these, never to a guessed default). SpeculativeMode Speculative-decoding mode, values mirror pvx_spec_mode_t exactly. Fail-closed rule: a configured path that cannot be honored (missing/unloadable draft model, missing capability, wrong vocab family) is a typed error naming the boundary — never a silent fallback to non-spec generation. SpeculativeType Supported speculative-decoding types, mirrored from the llama.cpp speculative enum via the engine's self-report (PVX_SPEC_TYPE_* bits). The ENGINE decides what the loaded MODEL supports — query IInferenceModel.SpeculativeCapabilities per model load and offer exactly these types for sequential mode; never assume.

docs/CAPABILITY.html.summary: ProvostXInference — Capability & Integration Guide What It Is A C/C++ inference engine that links llama.cpp directly and exposes a flat C API for P/Invoke from C#. Replaces LLamaSharp entirely. No wrapper, no managed/native split — we own the entire inference path. Current State (2026-09-25) 14/14 tests passing on macOS Metal (Apple Silicon, desktop-class) Library size: 11.3MB (statically links llama.cpp + ggml + mtmd) llama.cpp: latest master (e351231c4) Build: cmake with Metal/CPU/CUDA/Vulkan backend flags Capabilities Model Management pvx_load_model — load GGUF model with GPU layers, threads, flash attention, KV cache type pvx_free_model — free model pvx_load_mmproj — load vision projector (mmproj GGUF) → mtmd context pvx_free_mmproj — free vision projector Context pvx_create_context — create llama_context with n_ctx, n_batch, n_seq_max, pooling Presence penalty EOS detection Logits are copied before modification — no corruption of shared internal state Embeddings pvx_get_embeddings — text → normalized embedding vector Pooling modes: MEAN, CLS, LAST (configurable per context) L2 normalization pvx_embedding_dim — query embedding dimensions Vision / MTMD pvx_load_mmproj — load mmproj file → mtmd_context pvx_conversation_prompt_with_images — full pipeline: Decode image bytes (PNG/JPEG) via mtmd_helper_bitmap_init_from_buf Tokenize prompt + images into chunks via mtmd_tokenize Text chunks → queue as pending tokens Image chunks → encode via mtmd_encode_chunk → get float embeddings Flush pending text tokens (causal decode) Set non-causal attention → decode image embeddings via embd batch Restore causal attention pvx_mtmd_marker / pvx_mtmd_marker_static — get the media marker string pvx_mtmd_needs_non_causal — check if model requires non-causal for images pvx_set_causal_attn — per-call causal attention control Granular KV Cache Manipulation (impossible via LLamaSharp) pvx_conversation_shift_left / pvx_executor_shift_left — sliding window context: remove oldest N tokens, keep recent ones, continue generating without reset. RoPE positions stay correct via separate n_kv_pos tracking. pvx_kv_copy — copy KV from one seq_id to another (state backup without blob serialization) pvx_kv_clear_seq — clear one seq_id's KV without affecting other conversations pvx_set_causal_attn — toggle causal/non-causal attention per-call State Save/Restore pvx_state_save — snapshot KV to backup seq_id (via llama_memory_seq_cp) pvx_state_restore — restore from backup seq_id pvx_conversation_save / pvx_conversation_restore — per-conversation state Key improvement: No blob serialization, no managed/native split, one atomic operation Anti-Prompt Detection pvx_check_anti_prompts — check if generated text contains any anti-prompt string Thread Safety Internal std::mutex infer_mtx on every context serializes ALL native llama.cpp calls Pool has its own mutex for lease/return C# layer handles per-session SemaphoreSlim gates and cycle coordination What Needs Careful Handling at the C# Layer 1. Vision Processing (Single, Non-Batchable) The constraint: Image embeddings require non-causal attention (llama_set_causal_attn(ctx, false)). This is a context-wide flag — it affects ALL conversations on that context, not just the one with the image. What this means for the C# layer: pvx_conversation_prompt_with_images must be called inside the cycle gate (the _cycleGate SemaphoreSlim in BatchInferenceCoordinator) No other conversation can be decoding on the same context while image embeddings are being processed The C++ layer handles the causal/non-causal toggle internally, but the C# layer must ensure exclusive access during the call Flow: C# acquires _cycleGate → C# calls pvx_conversation_prompt_with_images(conv, mmproj, text, images) → C++ flushes text tokens (causal decode) → C++ sets non-causal → C++ encodes image (CLIP) → C++ decodes image embeddings (non-causal) → C++ restores causal → C# releases _cycleGate → Other conversations can now batch normally Cannot batch multiple conversations' image decodes in one llama_batch because: Text tokens need causal attention Image embeddings need non-causal You can't mix them in one llama_decode call Multiple images COULD be batched (both non-causal), but the CLIP encoding is the bottleneck and mtmd_batch_encode already handles that 2. Shift Left (Sliding Window) — Position Tracking The constraint: After shift_left(n), the logical token count (n_tokens) decreases but the absolute KV position (n_kv_pos) stays the same. RoPE positions in the remaining KV entries are absolute and must not be reindexed. What the C# layer must track: n_tokens (logical) — for headroom checks, overflow detection, max_tokens clamping The C++ layer handles n_kv_pos internally — C# never needs to know it After shift_left, the C# layer must re-evaluate headroom: headroom = context_size - n_tokens - safety_margin The C# layer should call shift_left BEFORE the context is full, not after — e.g., when n_tokens > context_size * 0.8, shift left by 10-20% of context size When to use shift_left vs reset: shift_left: Conversation is long but still relevant. Remove oldest tokens, keep recent context. No re-prompt needed. reset: Conversation is done or corrupted. Clear everything. Must re-prefill. 3. Repeat Penalty in Batch Mode The constraint: pvx_conversation_sample does NOT apply repeat penalty in batch mode (passes empty recent_tokens). The C++ layer doesn't track per-conversation token history for batch conversations. What the C# layer must do: Track recent generated tokens per BatchSession in C# (already done via _exactTokenCount and the session's prompt history) If repeat penalty is needed in batch mode, either: Option A: Pass recent tokens from C# to a new pvx_conversation_sample_with_history function (TODO if needed) Option B: Apply repeat penalty at the C# level by post-processing the sampled token (not ideal — can't modify logits after sampling) Option C: Accept no repeat penalty in batch mode (current approach — acceptable for most use cases) 4. Pool Exhaustion The constraint: The pool has exactly SeqMax conversations. If all are leased and a new request comes in, pvx_pool_lease returns PVX_ERR_NO_SLOT. What the C# layer must do: Set SeqMax = max_sessions in the config (already done) When PVX_ERR_NO_SLOT is returned, either: Queue the request and retry when a conversation is returned (preferred) Return HTTP 503 (service unavailable) to the client Do NOT create new conversations on the fly — that would exhaust seq_ids (the original bug) 5. State Save/Restore with n_seq_max == 1 The constraint: pvx_state_save copies KV to backup seq_id 1. If n_seq_max == 1, there's no backup seq_id. What the C# layer must do: For the standard executor (non-batched), set seq_max >= 2 so state save/restore works For batch mode, seq_max = max_sessions (always >= 2), so this is a non-issue If n_seq_max == 1 and state restore is called, the C++ layer returns OK with n_tokens = 0 — the C# layer must re-prompt the conversation 6. Thread Safety Model The C++ layer guarantees: infer_mtx serializes all native llama.cpp calls within a context Pool mutex serializes lease/return The C# layer must guarantee: Per-session SemaphoreSlim(1,1) request gate — only one request per session at a time BatchInferenceCoordinator._cycleGate — serializes the drain+infer cycle Vision prompt calls are made from the cycle coordinator thread (under the cycle gate) No concurrent calls to pvx_conversation_prompt_with_images and pvx_infer on the same context 7. Error Recovery On decode failure (PVX_DECODE_FAILED): The C++ layer does NOT modify n_tokens or n_kv_pos on failure The C# layer should: Log the error Call pvx_conversation_reset to clear the KV (safe — just llama_memory_seq_rm) Re-prompt the conversation from scratch Or call pvx_conversation_rewind to try removing the last prompt On pool exhaustion (PVX_ERR_NO_SLOT): Queue the request, don't crash Return 503 to the client with a Retry-After header On model load failure (PVX_ERR_LOAD_FAILED): Check pvx_last_error for the native error message Common causes: wrong path, corrupted GGUF, insufficient VRAM for requested GPU layers Build Matrix Platform Backend CMake Flag Tested? macOS arm64 Metal PVX_BACKEND_METAL=ON ✅ 14/14 macOS arm64 CPU (default) ✅ (implied) Linux x64 CPU (default) ⏳ CI Linux x64 CUDA PVX_BACKEND_CUDA=ON ⏳ CI Linux x64 Vulkan PVX_BACKEND_VULKAN=ON ⏳ CI Windows x64 CPU (default) ⏳ CI Windows x64 CUDA PVX_BACKEND_CUDA=ON ⏳ CI Windows x64 Vulkan PVX_BACKEND_VULKAN=ON ⏳ CI Backend Safety Layer Automatic detection, probing, and fallback for all GPU backends. No hardcoded assumptions — everything is verified at runtime.
