docs/CONFIGURATION.html.title: ProvostXInference — Configuration Reference | ProvostXInference API
docs/CONFIGURATION.html.summary: ProvostXInference — Configuration Reference Summary: ProvostXInference (PVX) is a C/C++ inference library with C# bindings, wrapping llama.cpp. The product code reads zero environment variables — all configuration is passed programmatically via C API structs by the embedding application (e.g., the ProvostX LLM server). Test/benchmark code reads three PVX_* env vars for model paths. Product Code: Environment Variables None. A grep of src/*.cpp and csharp/**/*.cs (excluding tests) for getenv / GetEnvironmentVariable returned zero matches. All PVX behavior is controlled by programmatic parameters set by the caller. This was confirmed by audit on 2026-09-26 and remains true as of 2026-09-27. Product Code: C API Programmatic Parameters These structs are the "knobs" embedders set when calling the PVX C API. They are not env vars — they are passed directly to pvx_load_model, pvx_create_context, and pvx_executor_sample / pvx_conversation_sample. pvx_model_params_t (passed to pvx_load_model) Field C Type Default What it does model_path const char* — (required) Path to GGUF model file gpu_layers int — GPU layers to offload. -1 = all, 0 = CPU only threads int — CPU threads. -1 = auto-detect flash_attn bool — Enable Flash Attention kv_cache_type pvx_kv_type_t — KV cache quantization: F16, Q8_0, Q4_0, Q4_1 reasoning_markers const char** NULL → built-in {" think"} Tag strings probed against vocab to detect thinking-capable models. First single-special-token match drives empty-block prefill when enable_thinking=0 n_reasoning_markers int <=0 → built-in default Count of reasoning marker strings pvx_context_params_t (passed to pvx_create_context) Field C Type Default What it does context_size uint32_t — Context window size (n_ctx) batch_size uint32_t — Batch size for decode (n_batch) seq_max uint32_t — Max concurrent sequences (batch mode pool size) pooling_type pvx_pooling_type_t — Embedding pooling: NONE, MEAN, CLS, LAST pvx_sampling_params_t (passed to sample functions) Field C Type Default (C# SamplingConfig) What it does temperature float 0.3 Sampling temperature top_p float 0.95 Nucleus sampling top-p top_k int 40 Top-k sampling. 0 = disabled min_p float 0.0 Min-p filtering threshold repeat_penalty float 1.1 Penalty for repeated tokens repeat_last_n int -1 Window size for repeat penalty. -1 = full context penalty_present float 0.0 Presence penalty max_tokens int 256 Max tokens to generate ignore_eos bool false If true, EOS token is not treated as end-of-generation C# Managed Defaults (record defaults) Record Field Default ModelConfig GpuLayers -1 (all) ModelConfig Threads 0 (auto) ModelConfig FlashAttention true ModelConfig KvCacheType F16 ContextConfig ContextSize 4096 ContextConfig BatchSize 512 ContextConfig SeqMax 4 ContextConfig PoolingType None Logging (Programmatic, not env-var) Knob API Default What it does Log callback pvx_set_log_callback(NULL) NULL (zero-overhead) Sets a global C callback for structured logs. NULL = no logging at all Min log level pvx_set_log_level(level) PVX_LOG_DEBUG Messages below this level are not dispatched. Levels: DEBUG < INFO < WARN < ERROR < NONE Test-Only Environment Variables These are read only by the C# test suite (SmokeTests.cs). They are never read by product code. Variable Type Default What it does PVX_MODEL_PATH string (env) ./models/Qwen3.5-4B-Q4_K_M.gguf Path to the main GGUF model used by smoke tests PVX_EMBED_MODEL_PATH string (env) ./models/all-MiniLM-L6-v2-Q5_K_M.gguf Path to the embedding model for embedding tests PVX_MMPROJ_PATH string (env) ./models/mmproj-Qwen3.5-4B-BF16.gguf Path to the multimodal projector for vision tests Status: Current as of 2026-09-27. Product code has zero env-var-driven behavior. All runtime configuration is programmatic via C API structs set by the embedding application.

docs/api-glossary.html.title: ProvostXInference — API Glossary | ProvostXInference API
docs/api-glossary.html.summary: ProvostXInference — API Glossary Every public type a consumer can touch, one purpose paragraph each, with the members that matter. Types are listed by layer; the consumer-facing set is deliberately small. Engines layer (the consumer surface) InferenceEngineBuilder (static) Entry point for every consumer. InferenceEngineBuilder.Gguf(path) / .Decision(path) / .Encoder(path) starts a typed request builder; With* methods add parameters; Build() returns a validated EngineRequest. Fail-closed: invalid combinations throw InvalidEngineRequestException before any native work. InferenceEngineFactory Constructs IInferenceEngine from a validated request. The default instance needs no configuration (parameterless). IInferenceEngine (interface) One loaded-or-unloaded engine object. Initialize() loads it (failure leaves it unloaded and disposable); Gguf / Decision / Encoder return typed ops views; Dispose() tears down in the fixed order pool → context → model. IGgufEngineOps (interface, via GgufEngineOps) The GGUF lane view: chat template, tokenize/detokenize, sampling, RebuildContext(), KV copy/clear, checkpoints, rewind/shift, speculation (ValidateSpeculation/EnableSpeculation/DisableSpeculation + ActiveSpeculation), vision encoder load, TTS session create, rerank, LoRA/cvec, Backend probe, GetExecutorStats / GetConversationStats (per-lane EngineStats), GetEngineTelemetry() (model-wide EngineTelemetry), CreateExecutor(), Pool (lazy IConversationPool). IDecisionEngineOps / IEncoderEngineOps Decision lane (ONNX judge session) and encoder lane (vision embedding route). Wrong-kind access throws EngineKindMismatchException. EngineLogging (static facade) Process-wide native DEBUG stream: SetLogFile(path) (native file sink), Enable(handler) (managed (level, tag, message) callback), SetLevel(0..3, 99). Distinct from the per-engine audit trail (see ModelConfig.AuditPath). EngineMaintenance (static facade) File-level engine-bound maintenance without a loaded engine: GGUF EOG/special-token metadata repair. StallWatchdogOps (static facade) Sole construction seam for the stall-safe prefill helpers (IPrefillStallDetector, IStallRecoveryLadder, IChunkWallClock). Abstractions layer (implemented by the native wrappers) IStandardExecutor Single-session generation: Prompt(text), PromptTokens(...) (feed-back during generation), Infer() → InferResult, Sample(SamplingConfig) → token, GenerateSpeculative(...), SaveState()/RestoreState(), GetStats(), EnableSpeculation(SpeculativeConfig), PromptWithAudio(...). IConversation / IConversationPool Pooled batched lane. Pool: Lease() / return-by-dispose, AvailableCount. Conversation: prompt/sample/grammar (SampleWithGrammar), SaveState()/RestoreState, ExportCheckpoint()/ImportCheckpoint() (byte-exact blobs), Rewind, Reset, GetStats(), SpeculationStats(). IInferenceContext Per-model decode context: Tokenize/Detokenize/TokenToPiece/IsEos, CreatePool(), CreateExecutor(), KV ops (KvCopy, KvClearSeq), ContextSize, SeqMax. IInferenceModel Model handle surface: CreateContext(ContextConfig), GetEmbeddings(ctx, text), EmbeddingDimension, LoadVisionEncoder(mmprojPath), ApplyChatTemplate(...), CreateGrammar(...) / CreateGrammarFromJsonSchema(...), SpeculativeCapabilities, CreateLoraAdapter(path), SupportsAudioInput, AudioSampleRate, PartialRewindSupported. IVisionEncoder Vision pipeline handle: Marker (prompt splice token) — used with PromptWithImages(prompt, encoder, imageBytes). ITtsSession Single-shot speech generation: Generate(text, params) → PCM F32 samples + rate; second generate refuses typed (tts/session-consumed); fresh sessions replay byte-identically per (text, seed). IGrammar Grammar handle (GBNF or schema-derived; Kind reports which). Owned by the sampled lane; dispose after the executor/conversation. Models layer (config records and snapshots) Record Purpose ModelConfig Model load knobs: Path, GpuLayers (-1 all / 0 CPU), Threads, FlashAttention, KvCacheType, context-pointer fields (wave-5: kv overrides, lazy mode, tri-states, LoadMtp), AuditPath/AuditIncludePrompts (ABI v9 audit) ContextConfig Context knobs: ContextSize, BatchSize, SeqMax, PoolingType, recurrent-state ring (NRsSeq), wave-5 extensions SamplingConfig Full pipeline: temperature/top-k/top-p/min-p, penalties, dry/xtc/top-n-sigma/mirostat, MaxTokens, grammar pointer SpeculativeConfig Mode (draft-simple, n-gram family, EAGLE3, draft-MTP), draft/companion paths, n-gram params StallWatchdogConfig Watchdog knobs: enabled, chunk size, gap multiplier, ladder budget EngineStats Per-lane snapshot: Tokens, KvPositions, PromptTokens, DecodeSteps, SpecDrafted, SpecAccepted EngineTelemetry Model-wide snapshot (ABI v9): PromptTokens, DecodeSteps, CommittedTokens, SpecDrafted, SpecAccepted, Errors, ContextsAlive BackendInfo Probe truth: backend type/name, EffectiveGpuLayers/requested, GpuLayersReduced, ProbePassed Exceptions layer Type Meaning InferenceException every native-side failure; ErrorCode + message + named boundary InvalidEngineRequestException builder request validation failure EngineKindMismatchException ops-view/kind mismatch PrefillStallUnrecoveredException watchdog ladder exhausted (carries chunk index, walls, steps) Enums & small types InferResult (Ok/NoWork/DecodeFailed), KvType (F16/Q8_0/Q4_0/Q4_1), PoolingType (None/Mean/Cls/Last/Rank), SpeculativeType/SpeculativeMode (draft/ngram family/mtp/eagle3/dflash), GrammarKind (Gbnf/JsonSchema), AudioChunk (PCM F32 + rate).

docs/contract.html.title: ProvostXInference — Consumer Contract | ProvostXInference API
docs/contract.html.summary: ProvostXInference — Consumer Contract Audience: developers of consumer services (ProvostXLLM, tools, tests). This is the stability promise of the caller-facing surface: what you may touch, what is guaranteed, and what is closed. Anything not listed here is internal and may change without notice. 1. The only entry point using ProvostXInference.Engines; // builder, factory, ops views, helper facades using ProvostXInference.Models; // config records, EngineStats, EngineTelemetry var engine = InferenceEngineBuilder.Gguf(modelPath) .WithGpuLayers(99) .Build(); // validated EngineRequest, fail-closed engine.Initialize(); var ops = engine.Gguf; // typed view; wrong kind => EngineKindMismatchException You reference exactly two namespaces: ProvostXInference.Engines and ProvostXInference.Models. Everything else (Implementation, Interop, SafeHandles, Logging, Abstractions) is a closed black box. 2. Engine object lifecycle contract Step Guarantee Builder.* → Build() Request validated fail-closed; bad paths/kinds/environments throw typed exceptions before any native work Initialize() Engine loads; failure leaves the engine unloaded and disposable — no partial state leaks engine.Gguf / .Decision / .Encoder Typed views over ONE graph; views wrap, never duplicate Dispose() Teardown in fixed order (pool → context → model); safe to call twice; safe after failed load 3. What IGgufEngineOps guarantees Model/context graph: chat template, tokenize/detokenize, sampling knobs, live context rebuild (RebuildContext() — old pool is disposed, state is not preserved), KV copy/clear, checkpoints (export/import byte-exact), rewind, shift. Backend probe: Backend reports the TRUTH — active specialist, effective/requested GPU layers, reduced flag. It never reports CPU for an active accelerator. Stats & telemetry (ABI v9): GetExecutorStats(executor) / GetConversationStats(conv) — per-lane counters (prompt tokens, decode steps, committed tokens, spec drafted/accepted). Snapshot copy-out; rejected drafts derive as drafted − accepted. GetEngineTelemetry() — model-wide snapshot for THIS engine instance: EngineTelemetry(PromptTokens, DecodeSteps, CommittedTokens, SpecDrafted, SpecAccepted, Errors, ContextsAlive). Pull-based and per-engine — derive rates between two snapshots in the caller; the engine keeps no rate state. Speculation: capability self-report (SpeculativeCapabilities — supported-types list, not booleans), validate/enable/disable. Unwired capability ⇒ typed NOT_SUPPORTED naming the boundary. Never a silent plain-generation fallback. Grammar: CreateGrammar (GBNF) / CreateGrammarFromJsonSchema. Every sampled token passed a grammar check (tiered rejection sampling) — output always conforms. 4. Per-engine audit trail (ABI v9) Set on the builder via ModelConfig: Setting Meaning AuditPath (null/empty = off) JSON-lines audit file for THIS engine instance only AuditIncludePrompts also record prompt token counts (never prompt text) Guarantees: Per-engine isolation: two engines in one process write two independent files and keep two independent telemetry streams. Nothing is shared (test-pinned). Events: model_loaded, model_freed, context_created, context_freed, spec_enabled, spec_disabled, kv_cleared, kv_shifted — each {"ts", "seq", "event", "detail"?}, monotonic seq, flushed per line (survives hard kill). Content policy: prompt TEXT is never recorded. Audit logs are not a content sink. Zero cost when off: unconfigured engines execute one branch per commit and nothing else — no counters, no I/O. Best-effort by design: audit is observability, never a correctness dependency; an unusable path logs a warning and disables the sink (load still succeeds). 5. Process-wide debug logging vs per-engine audit EngineLogging.SetLogFile/Enable/SetLevel routes the native DEBUG stream (llama.cpp/ggml/Metal + pvx internal logs). This is process-wide by nature — one specialist module owns the log state. Use it for diagnostics. Use AuditPath for per-engine operation trails. The two are independent channels. 6. Error contract Every failure is a typed exception carrying an error code, message, and a named boundary (e.g. spec-engine/mtp-wiring, json-schema/parse, kv/rewind): Exception When InferenceException any native-side failure (load, decode, capability, marshaled refusals) InvalidEngineRequestException builder request failed validation EngineKindMismatchException wrong ops view for the engine kind PrefillStallUnrecoveredException stall watchdog exhausted its recovery ladder Refusals are always typed and named — never empty messages, never silent fallbacks, never process aborts on supported paths. 7. Stability rules ABI handshake: the native library version must match the binding; mismatch refuses to load. Struct layouts are size-pinned by tests. Append-only ABI: new fields are appended; a zeroed struct reproduces previous behavior bit-for-bit. Consumers compiled against an older surface keep working. No silent behavior changes: every capability boundary refuses typed instead of degrading. If a feature reports supported, it is verified by tests. Config validation is fail-closed: invalid configs are rejected at build time, never clamped silently. 8. What is NOT in the contract Anything under Implementation, Interop, SafeHandles, Logging, Abstractions Internal counters not surfaced through the stats/telemetry records Native C API details (the flat pvx_* surface) — consumers go through the facade Prompt text handling inside audit trails (explicitly excluded by policy) 9. Version history ABI Consumer-visible change v8 wave-5 config verbs, stats export, audio/TTS/rerank/LoRA/cvec v9 per-engine audit (AuditPath, AuditIncludePrompts) + pvx_engine_telemetry / GetEngineTelemetry()

docs/faq.html.title: ProvostXInference — FAQ | ProvostXInference API
docs/faq.html.summary: ProvostXInference — FAQ Real questions from development and integration. Answers are contracts, not marketing. 1. Why not just use LLamaSharp? LLamaSharp wraps llama.cpp but owns the seams we need to control: batching discipline, KV lifecycle, backend safety, and error typing. We link llama.cpp directly behind our own flat C API so every one of those surfaces is explicit, fail-closed, and test-pinned. The C# layer is strict OOP (one type per file, constructor injection, no statics in product code) — that is a deliberate architectural stance, not style. 2. What happens if the native library version doesn't match the C# binding? The engine refuses to load. The ABI version is handshake-checked at engine open (PVX_ABI_VERSION vs ExpectedAbiVersion); a mismatch is a fail-closed error, never a best-effort attempt. Struct layouts are size-pinned by tests (PvxAbiSizeTests) so a drift cannot pass silently. 3. Does one process support multiple engines with different models? Yes — that is a first-class scenario. Each engine instance owns its model, contexts, pools, and telemetry. Two engines write two independent audit files (per-engine audit, ABI v9) and expose two independent GetEngineTelemetry() streams. Nothing is shared except the process-wide DEBUG log stream (EngineLogging), which is a single native log sink by design. 4. Does the audit trail record prompt text? No — by policy. The audit trail records lifecycle and operation events (model/context lifecycle, spec enable/disable, destructive KV ops) and optionally prompt token COUNTS (AuditIncludePrompts). Prompt text is never written: audit logs must not become a content sink. If you need content, that belongs in your service layer. 5. What does the audit feature cost when I don't configure it? One branch per commit. Every counter bump and every file write is gated behind audit.enabled; an unconfigured engine executes no counters and no I/O. The feature is dead when not actively set up. 6. A capability reports "supported" but I get a NOT_SUPPORTED exception — why? You are likely outside a documented lane boundary. Speculation, for example, self-reports capability per MODEL, but some modes are sequential-executor-lane only (the batched/pool conversation lane refuses typed). Every refusal names its boundary (e.g. spec-engine/mtp-wiring, spec-engine/session). The refusal is the contract: the engine never silently falls back to plain generation. 7. Which specialist backend is actually running? Ask the engine: ops.Backend reports the active specialist, effective vs requested GPU layers, and whether the load was reduced. The probe never misreports an active accelerator as CPU (a historic bug, fixed and pinned by tests). On macOS the metal specialist is the default; Linux/Windows default to cuda → vulkan → cpu in order of availability. 8. How do I get throughput numbers (tokens/second)? Telemetry is pull-based and stateless: take two GetEngineTelemetry() snapshots around your workload and derive rates in your code (DecodeSteps or CommittedTokens divided by elapsed time). The native side deliberately keeps no rate state — snapshots stay cheap and allocation-free. 9. Can I resume a conversation after a process restart? Yes — ExportCheckpoint() produces a byte blob (cells + K/V rows) that ImportCheckpoint() restores on a fresh engine, with token counts matching exactly. Verified across dense and hybrid architectures up to the largest test models. 10. Why are model files not in the repository, and why do live tests "skip"? Models are gigabyte-scale artifacts; the repo ships none (and no native binaries — CI builds every platform slice). Live test lanes discover models via PVX_SMALL_*_PATH env vars or repo-relative fixture locations; when a fixture is absent the lane skips with a named reason instead of failing. The suite is fully green with zero fixtures present (hermetic mode). 11. Is Windows / Linux really supported, or just macOS? All three build and test in CI (specialist matrix: osx-arm64 metal, win-arm64 cpu, win-x64/linux-x64 cuda+vulkan, plus a full Windows MSVC lane). The real-model journey tier has been verified live on ARM64 Linux and Windows lab VMs. CUDA/Vulkan specialists are CI-built but their real-model verification awaits a GPU host with models — that is stated openly in the backlog, not hidden. 12. What does "fail-closed" mean in practice? A failure or an unknown state produces a typed error that names what happened and where — it never produces a guessed result. Examples: unknown engine id → refusal listing known specialists; grammar with an unsupported JSON-schema keyword → NOT_SUPPORTED naming the keyword; rewind on a hybrid architecture → REWIND_UNSUPPORTED. We consider a silent wrong answer worse than a loud refusal.

docs/spike-BL01-ggml-isolation.html.summary: BL-01 · ggml multi-backend isolation spike — Verdict: GREEN (2026-10-09) Summary: ggml backend registries are PER-IMAGE statics, not shared globals — two specialist dylib images coexist in one process with zero registry pollution; Phase B per-handle tables unlocked (macOS slice proven). Evidence (all PASS, see spike/BL01Spike/spike-run.log) E1a dlopen dedupe: NativeLibrary.Load same path twice → identical handle (7a7fd3d0) — de-duped to one image. E1b identical content, different path → DISTINCT handles (7a7fd3d0 vs 7a7e2af0) — dlopen keys on path, NOT content; specialist copies do not collapse. E2 two independently built specialist images coexist as distinct handles (7a7fd3d0 / 7a7e2d70). E3 symbol routing: ONE DllImportResolver on the C# assembly, name→handle dict (pvxinferenceA→A, pvxinferenceB→B); pvx_abi_version returned 2 via both routes — no symbol collision, no interference. E4 registry isolation: image A's registry snapshot regs=[MTL,BLAS,CPU] devs=[MTL0,BLAS,CPU] identical before/after image B's full metal init — NO pollution, NO duplication (A still reports 3 regs, not 6). E5 registry pointer identity: ggml_backend_reg_get(0) A=166d5f898 vs B=16d6db3d0 — SEPARATE registry instances. Repro spike/BL01Spike/ (scratch .NET 10 console; NOT wired into product). Run: spike/BL01Spike/run.sh (env SPIKE_A, SPIKE_B = two built specialist dylib paths). Tested with build-metal-rel + build-metal2 metal specialists (osx-arm64, Apple Silicon desktop-class); both fully initialized metal (35 embedded metal libs each, ~2.5s + cached). What Phase B CAN assume (macOS-proven) Two same-specialist dylib images coexist via dlopen path-keying; registry/symbol state is per-image. Per-handle function tables + per-assembly resolvers can route logical names to distinct images safely. Registry of image A is untouched by image B's load — fail-closed per-handle dispatch is sound. What remains UNPROVEN macOS metal + cuda/vulkan cross-specialist pair: no vulkan/cuda specialist built locally — cross-backend registry semantics per-OS (Windows/Linux) need the BL-02 CI matrix builds. dlopen path-keying and registry-per-image statics are ggml structural properties and are expected to hold, but only the metal+metal pair was executed. Windows: .NET on Windows uses LoadLibrary, not dlopen — same-path dedupe and copy-path distinctness should map, but is untested on Windows. No token-exactness check in this spike (that is BL-02 acceptance). Rules Spike only; no product source touched; no merge to main. No identifying data anywhere.
